package_info.why_malicious: The package intentionally depends on every other public npm package, creating millions of transitive dependencies. This causes denial of service (DoS) for anyone installing it, leading to storage exhaustion, build pipeline failures, and prevents package removal for any package it depends on. The intent is disruptive, not functional.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the package.json declares dependencies on every public npm package, causing npm to recursively fetch and install millions of packages, resulting in resource exhaustion and denial of service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: No legitimate package should depend on every other package in the registry. This behavior is designed to overwhelm the package manager and system resources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages declare only necessary dependencies. This package intentionally abuses the dependency mechanism for disruption.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case exists for depending on the entire registry.
key_indicators: Dependencies list includes all public npm packages

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, sub-packages split the dependency list into chunks, each depending on a subset of npm packages, but together covering the entire registry. This amplifies the DoS effect and circumvents npm's technical limits on dependency list size.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Splitting dependencies into thousands of sub-packages to cover the entire registry is a clear abuse of the package system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal sub-packages serve functional modularity, not to aggregate all possible dependencies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Large monorepos may use sub-packages, but never to this scale or purpose.
key_indicators: Thousands of sub-packages with systematic naming
Each sub-package depends on a large, non-overlapping set of packages
Collectively, sub-packages cover the entire registry

attack_chain.action: User installs the 'everything' package, triggering npm to resolve all dependencies.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initiates recursive installation of all public npm packages.

attack_chain.action: Sub-packages are installed, each pulling in a chunk of the registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exponentially increases the number of packages to install, overwhelming system resources.

attack_chain.action: System experiences denial of service: storage exhaustion, build failures, and package removal lock-in.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: disrupt npm ecosystem and cause operational headaches.

behavioral_signatures: package.json with dependencies on an unusually large number of packages
Sub-packages with systematic naming (e.g., everything-chunk-*) each with massive dependency lists
Installations that trigger recursive downloads of thousands or millions of packages
file_indicators: Sub-packages named everything-chunk-* or similar mass-generated patterns
network_indicators: Massive spike in npm registry requests during install
Unusual download patterns covering the entire npm registry
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Flag any npm package whose package.json declares dependencies on an abnormally large number of packages (e.g., >1000). Monitor for sub-packages with systematic, mass-generated names and large dependency lists. Alert on install processes that attempt to fetch an excessive number of packages from the registry in a single operation.
